2022 State election

Listen

The next Victorian State election will be held on Saturday 26 November.

Every vote counts, and your vote matters. Every election is a chance for you to have a say about who represents you on the issues that you care about.

Find candidates in your area

Search your address to find a list of candidates and how-to-vote cards for your area.

Search your enrolled address, then pick a result from the dropdown. It's best if you enter a full address rather than a general suburb, because parts of some suburbs may be in different electorates.

Voting options

Early voting is open. You can also apply for a postal vote.

Find voting centres     Other voting options

How to vote correctly

At this election you'll receive 2 ballot papers: a smaller one for the Lower House and a larger one for the Upper House. Find out how to correctly complete them for your vote to count.

How to vote correctly

Away from Victoria during the election?

If you’re going to be away during the election, you can still vote.

Away during the election?

  • Missed the enrolment deadline?

    If you missed the deadline you can still vote. Visit a voting centre to enrol and vote on the spot. Make sure you bring your ID, such as driver licence, learner permit, Australian passport, or a recent electricity bill or council rates notice in your name and showing your address. Let one of our voting centre staff know you are not enrolled and they can assist you.

    Early voting opens Monday 14 November.

    Find voting centres

  • How-to-vote cards

    A how-to-vote card shows how a candidate or group wants you to fill out your ballot paper. You don't have to follow how-to-vote cards if you don't want to.

    How-to-vote cards handed out within 400 metres of a voting centre on election day must be registered with us. This also applies to how-to-vote cards distributed by our mobile voting teams.

    How-to-vote cards distributed during the early voting period to not need to be registered. However, all how-to-vote cards must be properly authorised.

    How-to-vote card registration has closed.

    Find how-to-vote cards

  • Work at the election

    We need 15,000 people to run this election. Will you join us?

    Many jobs involve working in a voting centre, but there are also positions available before and after election day.

    If you’ve worked with us in the past, let us know if you’re available this November.

    Apply to work at the election

  • Sort fact from fiction this election

    False or inaccurate information can easily spread online, sometimes unintentionally. It's important to think carefully about all electoral information you see this election.

    Read some tips on how you can sort fact from fiction in this election, and see a list of common election myths along with the facts in our misinformation register.

    Sort fact from fiction


  • Campaigning

    For voters

    During an election campaign, candidates will make statements about what they will achieve if you elect them. If you want to learn more about their policies, or ask questions, you can contact them directly. You can also check their social media or website for more information on their policies. 

    There are no laws requiring candidate or party advertising to contain their logo, party colours, or other branding. 

    Contact details for all candidates at the 2022 State election will be available on this website once the nominations period has ended at 12 noon on Friday 11 November. 

    Candidate conduct

    Candidates in an election campaign must obey electoral and all other laws, such as defamation law. Candidates must not distribute any material that is likely to mislead voters into voting incorrectly, such as how-to-vote cards that show an informal vote.

    If you think there has been a breach of the Electoral Act 2002 by a candidate or party, you can let us know using our Complaints and feedback page. 

    We cannot investigate claims made by candidates in their electoral campaign material unless it breaches legislation. 

    For candidates

    You can start campaigning at any time, even before nominations have opened.

    When campaigning, consider the following:

    • all electoral campaign material must be properly authorised so it is clear who is accountable for it
    • all non-electoral laws, such as those relating to defamation, still apply
    • you must not distribute material that is likely to mislead voters into casting their vote incorrectly
    • as soon as you publicly declare your intention to stand as a candidate, disclosure of political donations rules apply to you (even if you don’t end up nominating).

  • Get VoterAlert election reminders

    VoterAlert is our free SMS and email reminder service for voters in Victorian elections.

    Register now to get a digital EasyVote guide this November. After the election, we’ll let you know whenever there’s an election in your area, such as a by-election.

    To sign up, go to our ‘Check my enrolment’ portal. Once you have entered your details, subscribe for VoterAlert under the heading ‘Update contact details’. Simply add your mobile and/or email address and tick the related checkbox.

    Sign up in Check my Enrolment

    Find out more about VoterAlert

  • COVIDsafe election

    A State election is a major event where people come together to participate in democracy. Your health and safety and that of our staff is our top priority.

    We're putting a range of COVIDsafe measures in place this election to make sure you can vote safely and conveniently.

    Download our COVIDsafe election plan:

    • COVIDsafe election handbook 2022 (PDF, 386 KB)
    • COVIDsafe election handbook 2022 (Word, 1.2 MB)

    Your safety

    We'll be following the latest health advice to help minimise or stop the spread of coronavirus (COVID-19). Safety measures will be in place at all voting centres and with any activity that supports the election.

    Safety measures will include:

    • sanitising pencils between uses
    • hand sanitiser available at every voting centre
    • social distancing as appropriate.

    All election staff will need to show evidence of their COVID-19 vaccination status. They will need to have received 2 doses of a COVID-19 vaccine to work in a role with us for 4 weeks or less, and 3 doses to work with us for a longer duration.

    Vaccination requirements

    All enrolled Victorians will be able to vote in the State election, regardless of vaccination status. There are also no vaccination restrictions on candidates, scrutineers and party workers. 

    VEC employees will need to have 2 or 3 doses depending on the length of their appointment.

    Participant Vaccination requirement
    Candidate No requirement
    Party worker No requirement
    Scrutineer No requirement
    Voter No requirement
    Casual employee (up to 4 weeks) 2 doses
    Casual employee (4 weeks and over) 2 doses + 1 booster
    Ongoing employee 2 doses + 1 booster
  • If you are affected by the Victorian floods

    If you've been affected by the Victorian floods since 13 October, you have a range of voting options.

    Options for people affected by floods

  • Political donations

    Strict laws that regulate political donations in Victoria apply for the first time at this election.

    These include:

    • Only Australian residents, citizens, organisations or businesses can make political donations. Foreign donations are banned.
    • Donors cannot give more than $4,320 to any one recipient during the 4-year period between State elections.
    • Donors and recipients must disclose political donations of $1,080 or more in our VEC Disclosures portal within 21 days of making or receiving the donation. These donations cannot be anonymous.
    • Small donations ($54 or less) don’t have to be disclosed.

    There are serious penalties for breaking any of these rules.

    More about political donation rules

  • Troubleshooting advice

    We're aware of an issue impacting a small number of people trying to use our applications or online forms.

    We're working to resolve this as a priority.

    In the meantime, many people have solved the issue by following these steps:

    • close all tabs and windows for any VEC pages, apps or forms.
    • clear your cookies and cache (follow this guide to clear cookies and cache in every browser)
    • close your browser and/or restart your device
    • try to access the application or form again.

    Further things to check (advanced users):

    • Turn off settings that limit or hide IP address when browsing.
    • Temporarily turn off proxy or VPN services (to hide or change your apparent location).
